gbm_population_evidence.quote: Subjects must have histologically or cytologically confirmed WHO Grade IV Glioblastoma

candidate_evidence.quote: The purpose of this pilot study is to evaluate the addition of carvedilol with standard of care treatment to determine if it will improve progression-free survival in the front line setting in patients with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM).

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Subjects must have not received previous chemotherapy or radiation therapy for GBM
This is a pilot study to assess efficacy of the addition of a non-selective beta-blocker to standard of care treatment in the front-line setting of glioblastoma multiforme.

role_evidence.quote: Subjects will receive carvedilol starting at 6.25 mg orally (PO) twice daily for 1-2 weeks and if tolerated will then be increased to 12.5 mg PO twice daily starting on day 1 of concurrent chemoradiotherapy
Anti-Cancer Effects of Carvedilol With Standard Treatment in Glioblastoma
continue daily until the end of adjuvant cycle 6 of temozolomide and Tumor Treated Fields
Patients will be monitored with neuroimaging prior before chemoradiotherapy, before adjuvant temozolomide and every 2 months on adjuvant temozolomide.

biomarkers.biomarker_other: peripheral glioma circulating tumour cells (qRT-PCR / TelomeScan assay)

source_quote.quote: Quantify CTCs via qRT-PCR assay and to assess how the trend of CTCs correspond to disease status as measured by RANO criteria on neuro-imaging.

coder_notes: Registered EARLY_PHASE1 (translational subset). Temozolomide is not a registered intervention but the single arm receives standard chemoradiotherapy and adjuvant temozolomide, so it is listed as soc_backbone. TTFields (device) are part of the standard treatment and are not listed as an agent. CTC monitoring is a disease-response correlate, not linked to carvedilol's target, so target engagement coded no.
